note: Triennial rural district council election. Polling in Tyrone took place on Wednesday 31 May 1933. Nominations were received by Mr. John F. M'Crea, returning officer: nine Unionists and five Nationalists were returned unopposed, and two divisions had two nominations, Clogher (W. H. Boyd, Unionist, and Samuel Kirkpatrick, Ind. Unionist) and Augher (Impartial Reporter, 20 April 1933, p. 5). Augher was the only contest polled in the Clogher district, so one Clogher nomination was withdrawn; the withdrawal report has not been found, so Clogher division is not recorded. Labels are the paper's group headings. Filed on 1933-05-31, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Tyrone that year (confirmed). Vaughan, the official Unionist and retiring member; Richardson, an independent. Majority 83. Polling was quiet and there was considerable apathy among the Nationalist electorate.
